thread:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope for the client ergonomics + backoff proposal that ties into streaming. Customers (FinCo, EduCorp) have asked for predictable reconnect behavior and a simpler opt-in for adaptive backoff.
Alex Patel: Agree. High-level asks from product: 1) clear default for SDK that 'just works' for most users, 2) explicit escape hatches for enterprise, 3) nonbreaking for existing call patterns.
Ravi Singh: My draft RFC suggests a small surface: new RetryPolicy object + StreamingSession wrapper. Keeps old blocking SDK code unchanged.
Jamie Lee: Can you paste the code sketch here so we can eyeball ergonomics?
Ravi Singh: Sure — rough:
```
// Go example
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
// optional: use built-in resilient streaming
sess := client.StreamingSession( redwood.RetryPolicy{
  MaxRetries: 5,
  BackoffBaseMs: 200,
  MaxBackoffMs: 5000,
  Jitter: true,
  OnReconnect: func(ctx,reason){ /* app hook */ },
})
stream, err := sess.Open(context.Background(), opts)
```
Maria Chen: Nice. Product wants explicit acceptance criteria in the thread: what counts as 'launch'?
Samira Gomez: I'll propose a short list: (1) default SDK on-network reconnects <= 3s median for transient failures, (2) deterministic ordering/at-most-once semantics for application-visible events, (3) no change to sync/non-streaming APIs, (4) docs and migration guide + code samples.
Alex Patel: We should add telemetry requirements: events for reconnects, backoff used, final failure reason. That feeds Optimize and Console dashboards.
Ravi Singh: Telemetry planned: `stream.reconnect.count`, `stream.reconnect.reason`, `stream.backoff.ms` with tags for customer and model.
Jamie Lee: Edge cases: partial message re-delivery on reconnect, server-side idempotency, KV-cache mismatch for resumed requests. Need clear behavior: resume offset whenever server supports it, otherwise client must start fresh and surface a recoverable error.
Maria Chen: Can we avoid adding server changes? Product leaning to client-only first, but customers want resume. Prioritization question: do we ship client-only graceful reconnects and then later add resume protocol?
Alex Patel: Vote: client-only first (smaller blast radius). Offer advisory docs on how to implement idempotent app semantics. Then track resume server API as a follow-up.
Samira Gomez: Launch criteria (draft):
- Implementation in JS + Go + Python SDKs
- E2E tests simulating network blips (loss, DNS blip, TCP reset)
- Telemetry hooked into Console and a sample dashboard
- Migration docs + sample app with best-practices
- Feature flag for enterprise to disable auto reconnect
Ravi Singh: Technical acceptance criteria:
- Backoff algorithm respects jitter and caps, configurable per-session
- Reconnect attempts stopped after user context cancel or terminal error
- Streaming session exposes hooks: OnReconnect, OnBackoff, OnTerminalError
- No behavioral change to non-streaming methods
Jamie Lee: Testing matrix: unit tests for policy math, integration tests with flaky-proxy (we have that container), fuzz tests for rapid connect/disconnect, load tests to verify no herd behavior on reconnection.
Maria Chen: Docs/comms: docs-bot, please remind docs owners to draft quickstart with examples and migration checklist.
docs-bot: @Maria Chen — created docs ticket DOCS-512 and added Samira as assignee. :white_check_mark:
Alex Patel: Rollout plan: Canary in hosted for small sample (10% traffic) with telemetry alerts for reconnect spikes. If reconnects per-min > 2x baseline, auto-disable per-route.
Samira Gomez: Customer asks for config at organization and route level — we should spec policy precedence: route-level overrides org-level, then client default. Also expose env var for sysadmins.
Ravi Singh: Implementation note: keep policy as a serializable struct in config file + SDK constructors. Avoid magic environment parsing except for an explicit REDWOOD_STREAM_RETRY env for admins.
Jamie Lee: Backwards compat: default behavior should match current SDK (which currently retries minimally). So default MaxRetries should be conservative (e.g., 2) and product can raise it for beta.
Maria Chen: OK next steps: Ravi to update RFC with code samples and acceptance criteria, Samira to own telemetry + docs ticket, Alex to draft rollout playbook, Jamie to draft test matrix. Can we aim to merge RFC by next Tue?
Ravi Singh: I'll put an updated diff by EOD Fri.
Alex Patel: I'll schedule a 30m design review Mon to lock open questions (resume protocol, enterprise controls).
Samira Gomez: I'll line up customers for beta — FinCo and EduCorp volunteered.
Maria Chen: Thanks all! If anyone has blockers ping here. :rocket:
